docs.agreement.p1: The first time Unloop opens it shows its End User License Agreement, which is written in English. Read it to the end and Agree becomes available.
docs.agreement.p2: If you decline, Unloop is paused: nothing is arranged, and your audio still passes through unchanged. Choose Read it again whenever you are ready. Your answer is kept on your computer, for every copy of Unloop on it.
docs.agreement.title: The licence agreement
docs.automation.p1: Open Automation, pick a part and what to move, add a lane and draw on it. Each part has lanes for volume, pan, width, low-pass and high-pass cutoff, resonance, reverb and delay sends, drive, crush, gate depth and pitch; the master has volume and a low-pass.
docs.automation.p2: Draw points, or select and move them; bend the line between two; stamp a shape over a range — a ramp, an S-curve, a sine, triangle, square or saw, or random steps — and copy and paste a range. A move's own sweep or dive can be edited on the lane it plays. Automation is read sample by sample, live and in a print alike.
docs.automation.title: Automation
docs.capture.p1: After Generate, each instance captures one cycle of its loop — the music arriving on its track, never its own output — and from then on plays the record from memory. The LIVE / CAPTURED chip says where it stands, with Recapture and Forget capture. A loop longer than 64 seconds cannot be captured, and a stop, a jump or a tempo change during a capture starts it again at the next play.
docs.capture.p2: If the loop coming in is no longer the one captured, the chip asks: Loop changed — recapture? Nothing is replaced while it plays; recapturing is your press.
docs.capture.p3: With your DAW stopped, the play, pause, stop and loop keys in the master section — or the space bar — preview the whole record inside Unloop, every instance on the channel together. Click the map's ruler to jump, or loop a section. Press play in your DAW and it takes over at once.
docs.capture.title: Capture and preview
docs.fades.p1: Each end of a clip has three fade handles, as in Freally MIDI Master's Song Arrangement: the length on the clip's top edge and the curve on the fade itself. They never cross, at any clip length.
docs.fades.p2: Drag a clip's gain handle from −∞ to +6 dB — hold Shift for fine steps, double-click for 0 dB. The console has a fader for each part and a master fader. Every move is heard while you drag, and is one undo step when you let go.
docs.fades.title: Fades and faders
docs.generate.p1: Press Generate and Unloop plans the whole record for the name you picked: every section, which parts play in it, and every move. Choose a mode first — Radio cut, Mixtape cut, Club / DJ cut, Switch-up, Minimal and more, depending on the name — or leave it on Any mode and Unloop draws one.
docs.generate.p2: Every plan has a seed, 16 hexadecimal digits in the console, and each press of Generate draws a new one. The same loop, name, mode and seed always give the same arrangement: copy a seed to keep an arrangement or to send it to a collaborator, and paste one to get it back.
docs.generate.title: Generate, modes and seeds
docs.history.p1: Every change in the Song Arrangement view is one step of unlimited undo and redo. The Undo and Redo buttons at the top name the step, or press Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y). The history is saved with your DAW project.
docs.history.p2: Every change is also written to your computer at once, so if your DAW closes before you save, the project reopens on your last change and says so. If that change was really another copy's — an older project reopened after Save As — choose Keep the saved version.
docs.history.title: Undo, redo and autosave
docs.intro: This manual describes version 0.6.0, the version built today. Where something on the Features page arrives in a later version, the manual says which.
docs.keys.intro: Every edit in the Song Arrangement view works without a mouse. In Unloop, press <kbd>?</kbd> for this sheet; on a Mac, <kbd>Ctrl/⌘</kbd> is <kbd>⌘</kbd>.
docs.keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.language.p1: Unloop speaks eighteen languages. It starts in your system's language; to choose another, open Settings with the gear and pick one.
docs.language.title: Languages
docs.limits.display: On a second monitor at another display scale, the editor sizes itself from the primary display.
docs.limits.hands: Unloop has not yet been worked through by hand in every DAW, on every system. That is the release candidate's job, before 1.0.0.
docs.limits.midi: MIDI — the song template, MIDI loops and the Velocity Doctor — arrives in version 0.7.0. A loop's key is not known until then, so default file names leave the key out.
docs.limits.picture: A drag shows no picture of what you are dragging yet.
docs.limits.throw: A reverb or delay throw on the last bar is cut at the record's last bar line; the print does not ring on past it.
docs.limits.title: Known limitations
docs.name.p1: Type in the search to find any of 2,413 artists, producers and genres. Aliases and near misses find them too, and letters such as Ø, ß and Ł fold, so "mo" finds MØ. With the search empty it offers your recent names and the flagship models. Use the arrow keys and Enter, or click.
docs.name.p2: Each name has a model card: the modes it arranges in and how often each is drawn, its typical song forms, its signature moves, the parts it drives, where its data comes from and how confident it is. A name with little data of its own inherits from its genre, and the card shows the chain.
docs.name.title: Picking a name
docs.parts.p1: On one track with a finished stereo loop, Unloop arranges it in three bands — low, mid and high — and the map says so.
docs.parts.p2: For the full set of moves, put an instance on each part's track and give each one a role: drums, bass, melody, chords and so on. Unloop suggests one from the track's name. Instances on the same channel perform one record together: the first conducts, and every other follows its plan to the sample and plays only its own part's moves. The console shows a strip for each, with its fader and lamps.
docs.parts.p3: When your DAW runs plugins in separate processes, instances meet through a shared file on your computer, never the network. If another project's plan is already on a channel, Unloop says so and offers another channel.
docs.parts.title: One loop, or every part
docs.print.p1: PRINT in the master section opens Print & export. Choose what to print — the mix, the stems, any of the parts, a section or the whole record — and the format: WAV (16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float), AIFF, FLAC or MP3, at the captured sample rate or one you pick. It renders through the very code that plays live, so the file is what you heard. Cancel leaves nothing behind.
docs.print.p2: You can dither when the bit depth drops, put a safety limiter at −1 dBTP on the mix, and write receipts. File names come from a template you can edit, and by default no file name carries an artist's or producer's name. When the export is done, the print meter shows the mix's peak, true peak and loudness.
docs.print.p3: To skip the dialog, use the drag rack: drag the mix, the stems, one part or one section straight onto your tracks. The files are rendered before the drag begins, as 24-bit WAV by default.
docs.print.p4: A receipt, a small .unloop-receipt.json file, goes beside every export and every drag. It holds the versions, the name, mode and seed, and the fingerprints needed to make the same record again. Receipts are on by default; you can turn them off in the dialog.
docs.print.title: Print, drag and receipts
docs.privacy.p1: Unloop has no account and no telemetry, and the plugin and the standalone app contain no networking code at all. Your loops, your projects and your records never leave your computer, and a loop, a project or an export folder on a network drive is refused before anything on it is touched.
docs.privacy.p2: It keeps its own files in your app-data folder (%APPDATA%\Freally Unloop on Windows): the licence answer, your preferences, Recent Projects, the Loop Library's index, the capture cache (at most 2 GB) and the files instances meet through. It never writes into your loop folders; exports and projects go where you choose.
docs.privacy.p3: It contains no AI of any kind: every arrangement is planned by deterministic rules over researched arrangement data and performed by classic signal processing, and a build gate fails if a machine-learning library is ever added.
docs.privacy.title: Privacy and the network
docs.projects.p1: Save loop project… in the loop project menu (the folder button) saves the loop — its parts as 24-bit FLAC — with every arrangement over it, as one .unloop file. Open loop project… brings it back exactly. Saving never overwrites a file: a name that is taken gets (2).
docs.projects.p2: The Loop Library, in the same menu, lists every .unloop project and every WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and MIDI file in the folders you add, with its bars, tempo, tags and how often it has been arranged. Search and filter it; click a loop to hear it inside Unloop (the arrow keys walk the list, Esc stops), and Arrange it when it is exactly one loop. It only ever reads your folders. MIDI loops are listed now and become arrangeable in version 0.7.0.
docs.projects.p3: Make a loop from a longer file… cuts a loop out of a longer recording: pick a start bar, a length of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars and the tempo, hear the cut on repeat, then Arrange it as a new loop project. The file itself is never changed.
docs.projects.p4: Recent Projects lists what you opened or saved, newest first. One that has moved shows as missing, and Remove from list takes the row away — never the file.
docs.projects.title: Loop projects and the Loop Library
docs.reroll.p1: Lock a section or a clip you like, and Reroll draws the rest again. It never touches a locked section or a clip you edited, and never moves a neighbour. What changed then lists every part and move it changed, section by section.
docs.reroll.p2: Add move opens a palette of every move, this arrangement's own first: place one on the moves strip, then drag, stretch or delete it. Select a move to open its inspector — its start, its length, its parts and its own settings, such as a filter's range or a stutter's steps — and Audition it while the preview plays.
docs.reroll.title: Lock, reroll and moves by hand
docs.sections.p1: Open a section's menu from its header, or press M, to rename it, change its kind or its length, move it earlier or later, insert a new section before or after it, remove it or lock it. You can also drag a section to reorder it: everything in it goes with it.
docs.sections.title: Sections
docs.shelf.p1: The Arrangement menu holds every arrangement of the loop you have open: New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Switch — on the next bar while playing, at once when stopped — and Compare, an A/B between any two. Each arrangement keeps four snapshots, A to D: click one to recall it, or Shift-click to keep the arrangement there.
docs.shelf.p2: Export arrangement… writes one arrangement as an .unarr file, without its loop. Import arrangement… lays one over the loop you have open, finding each section, clip, move and lane by what it is, and lists anything that had no place.
docs.shelf.title: Many arrangements on one loop
docs.start.p1: Freally Unloop runs inside your DAW as a CLAP or VST3 plugin, or as an AU on macOS, and on its own as a standalone app. Put it on the track that plays your loop: until you press Generate it passes the track's audio through exactly as it arrives, so it is safe to leave in place.
docs.start.p2: Version 0.6.0 is built to be used in a DAW, with audio. MIDI arrives in version 0.7.0; arranging stems dropped into the standalone app, and the web app, arrive in version 0.8.0.
docs.start.p3: There are no downloads before version 1.0.0, and the source code is private.
docs.start.title: Getting started
docs.tempo.p1: In a DAW, Unloop always plays at your project's tempo and never changes it. The tempo chip says whether your tempo is in the range the name usually works at — counting half and double time as a match — and, if it is not, which tempo to set your DAW to, with a button to copy it.
docs.tempo.p2: Unloop needs to know how long your loop is: it asks, and assumes 8 bars until you say. The clock follows your DAW's song position, or counts the loops itself when the position does not move — FL Studio's pattern mode, or Ableton Live's session view — so the whole record still plays over a loop going round. Auto decides for you; choose Song or Loop to decide yourself.
docs.tempo.title: Tempo and the clock
docs.timeline.p1: Every clip on the map is yours to edit. Click to select it, Shift-click or drag a marquee for more, or press Ctrl/Cmd+A for all. Drag a clip to move it on the snap (hold Alt to move it freely), drag an edge to resize it — the loop repeats past its length — and Alt-drag inside it to slip it. S splits at the edit cursor.
docs.timeline.p2: The clip's menu — right-click, Shift+F10 or the menu key — holds Cut, Copy, Paste, Clone after, Duplicate in place, Delete, Split at the cursor, Reverse, Lock, Reset to plan, Colour and Rename. A clip pasted onto a lane its part cannot go on is offered the lanes it can.
docs.timeline.p3: Snap to the bar, the beat, an eighth or a sixteenth note, their triplets, or nothing; zoom in and out, or fit the whole record. Where clips meet, Unloop crossfades them over 3 ms, and with snapping off an edge lands on the loop's nearest zero crossing, so no edit makes a click.
docs.timeline.title: Editing the timeline
docs.window.p1: Along the top are the loop project menu (the folder button), the Arrangement menu, the search, the mode, and Undo and Redo; on the right, the tempo, the clock and Settings (the gear). In the middle is the arrangement map: the record's sections, a lane for each part, and its moves. Along the bottom is the console: Generate, a strip for each part, the master section and the seed.
docs.window.p2: Settings holds the language, the theme — System, Dark or Light — and the list of keyboard shortcuts.
docs.window.title: The window
featuresPage.cards.live.body: Press play and Unloop performs the record over your own audio, in time with your project: intros, hooks, drop-outs, 808 cuts, filter sweeps, stutter builds, tape stops, half-time and beat switches. No move clicks, and none adds latency.
featuresPage.cards.live.title: The whole record, performed live
featuresPage.cards.midi.body: Flip to MIDI and the same arrangement becomes a multi-track MIDI song template, read from your own loop's notes, with section markers. The Velocity Doctor gives each part the right kind of velocity: accents and ghosts on drums, a steady 808, even chords.
featuresPage.cards.midi.title: Audio or MIDI, one switch
featuresPage.cards.modes.body: A genre is arranged several ways — radio cut, mixtape cut, club cut, switch-up, minimal — unless it genuinely has only one, and then its card says why. Artists and producers add their own, and every press is a new seed you can keep and paste to get the same arrangement back.
featuresPage.cards.modes.title: Not one template per genre
featuresPage.cards.offline.body: No account, no telemetry and no model: a rule-based planner and classic signal processing, checked by a build gate. The plugin and the standalone never go online; the one exception is an update check that stays off unless you switch it on, run by a separate program.
featuresPage.cards.offline.title: Offline, private, no AI
featuresPage.cards.parts.body: One stereo loop is enough: Unloop arranges it in low, mid and high bands. Put an instance on each part's track instead and one of them conducts them all as one record, with a full console of faders and lamps.
featuresPage.cards.parts.title: One loop, or every part
featuresPage.cards.pattern.body: FL Studio's pattern mode and Ableton's session view loop without moving the song position. Unloop counts the loops itself, so the whole record still plays over the 8 bars going round.
featuresPage.cards.pattern.title: Even on a loop that never moves
featuresPage.cards.redream.body: Re-Dream gives three new takes on the arrangement you have, keeping its shape. Add synthesized risers and impacts, your own producer tag and beat switches, then let the Arrangement Doctor point out a late hook or a section that never changes, with a fix.
featuresPage.cards.redream.title: Re-Dream and the Arrangement Doctor
featuresPage.cards.search.body: 2,413 artists, producers and genres in one search, through aliases and typos. Before you press anything, a card says what that name does: its song forms, its ways of arranging, its section lengths and its signature moves.
featuresPage.cards.search.title: Search a name, not a genre
featuresPage.cards.shelf.body: Each loop is saved once, as its own project, with a shelf of named arrangements: switch between them on the next bar, compare any two, and carry one to another loop as a file. The Loop Library holds every loop you have, ready to audition.
featuresPage.cards.shelf.title: One loop, many arrangements
featuresPage.cards.standalone.body: Drop up to eight stems or MIDI files and arrange them without a DAW. With no DAW to follow, Unloop suggests the artist's tempo and can stretch your loop to it; the Loop Doctor finds seam clicks, clipping and a tempo that does not add up.
featuresPage.cards.standalone.title: A standalone app and a web app
featuresPage.cards.take.body: Preview the arrangement inside Unloop while your DAW is stopped. Print it as WAV, AIFF, FLAC or MP3, the mix or one stem per part, and drag the song, one part or one section straight onto your tracks. A receipt goes beside every file.
featuresPage.cards.take.title: Hear it, then take it
featuresPage.cards.timeline.body: Move, copy, split, resize and fade every clip with three-handle fades; ride clip, part and master faders; draw automation on 12 lanes per part; reorder sections; lock what you like and reroll the rest. Unlimited undo, and an autosave that survives a crash.
featuresPage.cards.timeline.title: The timeline is yours
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.0 does
featuresPage.coming.downloads: There are no downloads before version 1.0, and none on this page.
featuresPage.coming.intro: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. This page describes version 1.0, and Unloop is built one rung at a time, so not everything on it is built yet. Each rung on the road to 1.0 is marked with its state.
featuresPage.coming.title: What is still coming
featuresPage.compare.asOf: Unloop's column is version 1.0, which is not out yet, and its price is today's: Unloop is free today, and future versions may be sold. The other products change too; this table is as of 2 October 2026. Product names are trademarks of their owners, and Freally Unloop is not affiliated with any of them.
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally Unloop 1.0 next to five products sold today that arrange a loop, vary it or write whole songs: ArrangerKing (an arrangement plugin), Loopmix (a loop-remix plugin), Songen (a beat-making app), and Suno and SOUNDRAW (AI song generators). Every cell for another product comes from its maker's own pages, checked on 1 and 2 October 2026, and prices are US dollars before tax, as listed on 2 October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.note.nameStops: a name can stop a song
featuresPage.compare.price.suno: Free tier; Pro $10 and Premier $30 a month
featuresPage.compare.row.edit: Every clip, fade, fader and automation lane editable
featuresPage.compare.row.midi: The song as a MIDI file
featuresPage.compare.row.moves: Moves performed on your own audio: 808 cuts, stutter builds, tape stops
featuresPage.compare.row.styleOf: Arranges in the style of an artist or producer you name
featuresPage.compare.row.systems: Native on Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.compare.row.yourLoop: Turns your own loop into a whole song for you, writing no new music
featuresPage.compare.summary: The short version: only Unloop turns your own loop into a whole record for you, in the style of an artist or producer you name, with the moves performed on your own audio. It is the only one native on Linux as well as Windows and macOS, and the only one that works offline with no account, no telemetry and no AI.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Where they win: Suno, SOUNDRAW and Songen write new music for you — which Unloop never does, on purpose. Loopmix slices and resequences the inside of a loop rather than arranging it into a song, and it is also an AAX plugin for Pro Tools, which Unloop 1.0 is not.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side with the commercial tools
featuresPage.free.body: Everything Unloop does today is free, for everyone: no paid tier, no subscription, no account, no key, no ads and no trial that runs out. The arrangements, audio, stems and MIDI you make with it are yours, as far as the loops you arranged were yours to use.
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.lead: Freally Unloop turns an 8-bar loop into a finished, arranged record in the style of any of 2,413 artists, producers and genres — performed over your own sound, live in your DAW, then dragged out as audio stems or as a MIDI song template.
featuresPage.limits.aax: It is not a Pro Tools (AAX) plugin.
featuresPage.limits.bands: One stereo loop is arranged in three bands, so a move cannot pull a snare away from a melody. Give each part its own track for the full set of moves; when you print, a percussive and harmonic split helps, and Unloop says it is an approximation.
featuresPage.limits.daw: It is an arranger, not a DAW: no recording, no plugin hosting, and no mixer beyond its part and master faders.
featuresPage.limits.midi: Its MIDI from audio says what it cannot do: no countermelody from audio, chords spelled plainly, and a sung line left out rather than guessed.
featuresPage.limits.newMusic: It does not write new music. A new fill, or a second pattern for a beat switch, comes from you: Unloop arranges what is in your loop and adds only the transition effects it synthesizes.
featuresPage.limits.songs: It does not recreate a famous song's arrangement, and never will.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.0 does not do
featuresPage.numbers.flagships: flagship styles, down to their signature moves
featuresPage.numbers.formats: file formats out: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and MIDI
featuresPage.numbers.names: artists, producers and genres to arrange like
featuresPage.numbers.systems: operating systems: Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.version: This page describes Freally Unloop version 1.0: everything on it is in 1.0, and nothing planned for after 1.0 is on it.
featuresPage.why.local.body: No account, no telemetry, no cloud. Your loops and your records never leave your computer, and a build gate fails if network code reaches the plugin or the standalone. The web app loads once, then works offline and uploads nothing.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.rules.body: A planner reads researched arrangement data for each artist, producer and genre, and decides every section and move before a sound plays. The same loop, name, mode and seed give the same arrangement today and in five years — so a seed you send a collaborator plays them exactly what you heard.
featuresPage.why.rules.title: Rules you can read
featuresPage.why.sound.body: Every sound in an arranged record comes from your loop, or is a transition effect Unloop builds from oscillators and noise. It never writes a note of new music into your song, and never changes the loop file on your disk.
featuresPage.why.sound.title: Your sound, arranged — never replaced
featuresPage.why.styles.body: A name describes how someone arranges, and nothing more. Unloop never recreates a specific song's arrangement, and keeps names out of your file names unless you put them there.
featuresPage.why.styles.title: Styles, never songs
featuresPage.why.tempo.body: The plugin always plays at your project's tempo and never changes it. When the artist or producer you picked works at another tempo, Unloop suggests it, and counts half and double time as a match. In the standalone and the web app, it can stretch your loop to their tempo.
featuresPage.why.tempo.title: It follows your DAW
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is
featuresPage.why.views.body: The audio and the MIDI song template are drawn from the same plan, and every edit reaches both. When MIDI cannot say what a move did — a tape stop's pitch dive — the move is marked as audio-only instead of quietly dropped.
featuresPage.why.views.title: Two views, one truth
footer.licence: Proprietary — All Rights Reserved. © Mike Weaver. Free to use today; future versions may be sold. Not open source.
footer.yours: The music you make with Unloop is yours, as far as the loops you arranged were yours to use, with no royalty and no attribution required.
hero.headline: Your loop. Their arrangement. Your record.
hero.sub: Turn an 8-bar loop into a finished, arranged record in the style of any artist, producer or genre — performed live in your DAW, then dragged out as audio stems or as a MIDI song template. Free, offline, and 100% AI-free.
honest.bands.body: With only a finished stereo loop to work from, Unloop moves its low, mid and high bands, so a move cannot pull a snare away from a melody. Put an instance on each part's own track for the full set of moves.
honest.bands.title: One stereo loop is arranged in three bands
honest.downloads.body: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. An arranger that half-works is worse than one that is not there yet.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads before 1.0.0
honest.hands.body: Unloop is built and checked by automated gates on Windows, Linux and macOS. Working it through by hand in real DAWs, on every system, is the release candidate's job, before 1.0.0.
honest.hands.title: Not yet tried by hand in every DAW
honest.network.body: The plugin and the standalone app contain no networking code at all, and a build gate fails if any is added. A later version may add an update check that is off unless you switch it on, run by a separate program.
honest.network.title: It never goes online
honest.notes.body: Every sound in an arranged record comes from your loop, or is a transition effect Unloop builds from oscillators and noise. It decides when each part plays and performs moves on it, but it never writes a note of new music and never changes the loop file on your disk. A new fill, or a second beat for a switch, comes from you.
honest.notes.title: It arranges your music; it does not write any
honest.styles.body: Artist, producer and genre names are used only to describe musical styles. Freally Unloop is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by or approved by any artist, producer, label or rights holder, and it never recreates a specific song's arrangement.
honest.styles.title: Names describe styles
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
how.loop.body: Your 8 bars loop in the DAW — or drop stems or a MIDI loop into the standalone or the web app.
how.loop.title: Loop it.
how.name.body: Search 2,413 artists, producers and genres and choose a mode: every genre can be arranged several ways.
how.name.title: Pick a name.
how.play.body: Unloop performs the whole record over your own audio — intros, hooks, drop-outs, 808 cuts, stutter builds, tape stops, beat switches — in time with your project.
how.play.title: Press play.
how.shape.body: Move, copy, split and fade clips, ride faders, draw automation, lock what you like and reroll the rest.
how.shape.title: Shape it.
how.take.body: Drag out the arranged record as WAV, AIFF, FLAC or MP3 — mix or stems — or as a multi-track MIDI song template.
how.take.title: Take it.
how.title: How it works
ladder.intro: One line per version. This is the same ladder the private plan follows — if one moves, both move, and a build gate compares them.
ladder.note: A version that is done is built and tagged. It is not a download: there are none, and there will not be until 1.0.0.
ladder.rung.v0.1.0: The plugin (CLAP, VST3, AU) and the standalone load and pass audio; the editor shell, design tokens, 18 languages, every quality gate, local CI on Windows and Linux, plugin validators, browser tests.
ladder.rung.v0.10.0: Every genre in several modes, hundreds of flagship artists and producers, every name resolving honestly.
ladder.rung.v0.2.0: Any of 2,413 artists, producers and genres becomes a deterministic arrangement plan, with several modes per genre.
ladder.rung.v0.3.0: One instance on a looping beat performs the whole record live — clicks-free, zero latency, in sync with your DAW.
ladder.rung.v0.4.0: An instance per part, conducted as one record, with the full console.
ladder.rung.v0.5.0: Capture, preview inside Unloop, print to WAV/AIFF/FLAC/MP3, drag out, loop projects, and the Loop Library — browse, audition and cut your loops, reopen recent projects — the first complete product: the MVP.
ladder.rung.v0.6.0: Move, copy, split and resize clips; fades, faders and automation; lock and reroll; unlimited undo and redo; the arrangement shelf and .unarr files; every edit from the keyboard.
ladder.rung.v0.6.5: Knobs, faders and buttons rendered in Blender, five skins in light and dark, interface sounds and a dark title bar — the same in every Freally app.
ladder.rung.v0.7.0: Audio-to-MIDI, MIDI loops in, the MIDI song template, the Velocity Doctor, MIDI drag-out.
ladder.rung.v0.8.0: Stems mode in the standalone and the web app, tempo adhere, the Loop Doctor.
ladder.rung.v0.9.0: Re-Dream, synthesized transition FX, beat switches, the Arrangement Doctor, templates, MIDI learn.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: Downloads open, and the web app goes live.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-rc: Reviewed top to bottom with every bug fixed, then tested by hand in real DAWs on every system available — with the complete web app and this site finished.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0b: Feature-complete: edge cases, accessibility, 18 languages, performance budgets, installers for three systems.
ladder.title: The road to 1.0
shortcut.clipAbove: Select the clip on the lane above
shortcut.clipBelow: Select the clip on the lane below

shortcut.deselect: Select nothing, or let go of a drag
shortcut.endEarlier: Shorten the clip from its end
shortcut.endLater: Lengthen the clip at its end
shortcut.fadeDone: Let go of the fade handles
shortcut.fadeLonger: Lengthen the fade by the snap
shortcut.faderFineDown: Lower the fader a fine step
shortcut.faderFineUp: Raise the fader a fine step
shortcut.fadeShorter: Shorten the fade by the snap
shortcut.lock: Lock or unlock the selected clips
shortcut.moveDown: Move the selected clips to the lane below
shortcut.moveEarlier: Move the selected clips earlier by the snap
shortcut.moveLater: Move the selected clips later by the snap
shortcut.moveUp: Move the selected clips to the lane above
shortcut.preview: Play or pause the preview while your DAW is stopped
shortcut.startEarlier: Lengthen the clip at its start
shortcut.startLater: Shorten the clip from its start
site.tagline: Every loop is a record waiting to happen.
what.p1: A loop that sounds finished at bar 8 is still a loop at bar 64. Turning it into a record means hours of muting, copying, cutting and automating — the intro, the hooks, the drop-outs, the switch-ups — before you hear whether the idea holds up.
what.p2: Freally Unloop arranges it for you. Put it on the track that plays your loop, pick an artist, a producer or a genre, and press play: Unloop performs the whole record over your own audio, in time with your project, the way that name arranges.
what.p3: Then the record is yours. Edit it clip by clip, keep what you like and reroll the rest, and print it — the mix or one file per part — to drag straight onto your tracks.
